title: Who Said That

source.quote: An ego-state is a set of related behaviors, thoughts and feelings.

setting: Thursday, 4pm. Sprint retro. The release went out stable this time, and Dev, a senior engineer, agreed to the new deploy schedule two minutes ago.

L1.question: Dev agreed to the schedule two minutes ago, but something's shifted. Which ego state is he speaking from now?

options.feedback: He sounds like he's handing down a verdict, but a verdict is usually delivered with more energy than this flat compliance.
Adult agreement would sound like agreement - specific, maybe even a question. "Fine, whatever you say" with arms crossed is compliance, not agreement.
Right. The clipped "fine, whatever", the crossed arms, and the lifted chin are Adapted Child doing minimal compliance while registering a protest it won't say out loud.

L1.lesson: Ego state is a coherent set of behaviour, thought and feeling, not a single word. "Fine" can be said from any of the three states; here the clipped tone, crossed arms, and lifted chin all point to the same Child reading - that consistency across cues, not the word itself, is the diagnosis.

L2.intro: You (Priya) called this retro to close out the sprint clean, not to re-open an old fight. What do you say to Dev?

options.text: Great, glad we're on the same page.
options.outcome: Dev shrugs and goes quiet for the rest of the meeting. Nothing gets fixed.
options.lesson: Taking "fine" at face value when the cues say otherwise lets a Child protest go underground instead of getting named - the content was Adult-sounding, the cues weren't.

options.text: You don't sound fine. What's actually going on?
options.outcome: Dev's arms drop. "Honestly? Nobody asked if Friday even works for me." Now you have something to work with.
options.lesson: Naming the mismatch between words and cues from Adult invites the real content out - Berne's behavioural diagnosis means checking words against tone, posture and gesture together, not taking any one of them in isolation.

options.text: We already agreed on this, Dev.
options.outcome: Dev's jaw tightens. "Sure. Whatever you say." Same four words, same flat voice - the loop just repeats.
options.lesson: Meeting an Adapted Child protest with Controlling Parent pressure is complementary, so it keeps running - it quiets the protest without resolving it.

options.text: No worries, we can always change the schedule later if it's a problem.
options.outcome: Dev relaxes slightly. "Okay... thanks." But Friday is still never actually addressed.
options.lesson: Nurturing Parent softens the moment but doesn't ask what's wrong - it treats the symptom (tension) rather than the content (an unaddressed objection).

fields.label: Draw the vectors for Dev's "fine, whatever", and for Priya's best response.
In under 60 words: Dev's words sound almost Adult. Name two nonverbal cues that overrule the words, and say why cues win when they disagree with content.

echo.setting: 36 hours later: Leela, a new hire, texts back about a moved deadline.
echo.shape: same diagnose shape as L1 - flat text against a known pattern of cues
